measurement.note: The agreed target uses effective code LOC. Physical and nonblank line counts are independently reported and also exceed an 8% reduction.

changes.evidence: 58 historical migrations replaced by one V1 schema baseline. Removed one-time report conversion, Artifact resealing and upgrade-only tests. Profile seeding is transactional and runs once; report deletion retains row locking and running-report protection without taking the unrelated routing lock.
Controller Settings and delivered Runner revisions are the sole model configuration path. Removed environment bootstrap fallbacks and GUARD_OTEL aliases; standard OTEL settings remain.

Project-owned package schema, artifact digest, compiler IDs and Policy schema use V1. Built-in Policy and Profile pins use 1.0.0. Third-party format/model identifiers and user-created immutable revisions keep their actual semantics.

Removed bundled historical definitions and loaders, duplicate-ID replacement, retired Topic rules and the Topic upgrade UI. Retained all five current Profiles, the 748-case Default composition suite and full-feature baseline. Topic finding attribution now recognizes the current V1 Rule IDs.

Removed unreachable provider/endpoint UI, obsolete help URL aliases, old acceptance scripts and the one-time upstream importer. Removed the promotion harness that called deleted report APIs; current package import/export PostgreSQL tests remain. Current CLI smoke, live model/stream and report-memory harnesses remain.

Removed frozen migration-only baselines, historical Policy replay tests and old signed artifacts. Signed unsupported-contract tests now derive valid signatures from current fixtures and verify refusal before activation. Retained current regression cases under descriptive filenames and explicit Rule ownership assertions. ZIP invariants compare paths and native byte equality rather than recursively walking Buffer properties.
Removed superseded design and experiment diaries; updated retained links and V1 contracts. Upstream license/provenance notices remain. Data/document deletion is excluded from the LOC reduction.

Replaced the mechanical legacy-to-previous renames with domain-specific names and current behavior descriptions; restored the upstream character-entities-legacy package identity. Removed unused localization keys, old Secret-name copying and ConfigMap ownership adoption, Topic allowlist bypasses, and the archived P0 verifier. Current strict/permissive Topic modes require semantic review; unsupported modes are rejected.

controller_source_tests.note: All PostgreSQL test switches enabled against isolated PostgreSQL 17. Compiled dist directories excluded. Migration teardown owns its pool references and has an explicit cleanup budget.

python_non_e2e.resolution: The two failures were synthetic ordered-execution fixtures still pinning a removed Topic Policy version. Updated those fixture pins to current V1; the production code is unchanged after the full run. Entire ordered-execution module rerun recorded separately.

protocol_and_e2e.skip_reason: Actual Relay proxy tests require an explicitly configured isolated Relay image or Python installation.

policies.not_run_reason: Model-backed acceptance cases require configured live models; synthetic transport integration tests run separately.

intentional_boundaries: Existing development databases do not match this V1 baseline and must be initialized fresh; no existing database was changed. Unsupported signed artifacts require recompilation and package imports accept only V1.
Old environment model configuration, GUARD_OTEL aliases, bundled Policy history and old help URL aliases are not supported.
Runtime-log encryption, artifact/protocol signature and digest checks, immutable user Policy/Guardrail revisions, import provenance and bootstrap credential recovery remain current requirements.
Chart bootstrap handles current managed Secret names and Namespace ownership only. It does not copy obsolete Secret names or adopt ConfigMap-owned Secrets.
limits: Optional external Redis/Relay, database recovery and real Kubernetes lifecycle tests are not enabled by the general Python run. No existing deployment or Kubernetes resource was changed.
These results verify cleanup and behavior; they are not a new memory/concurrency benchmark or evidence of live-model detection quality.
